evidence: The agent probed 60,000 random palettes. Only bandItemFor's truecolor arm fired, so it pinned that one with a real palette (dbbf07d adds 'a band item drawn as its own plane throws'). It argued the other two arms were unreachable, so a test would fake ensureDrawn. The flag is a false positive: eaf44c9 was the head at the first finished review, and it only added a comment in planeNeighbours; the throw sites are original PR code.
guidance_note: When adding a throw site for a repair search, probe whether it is reachable with generated inputs before pushing, and pin each reachable one with a real input in the same PR.

evidence: The header comment says it lists 'every colour operation used' and added ensureDrawn, but drawnColour, which is imported and used, was missing; dbbf07d adds it. This is original PR content: eaf44c9 was the first-reviewed head and did not touch this line.
guidance_note: When editing a comment that claims to enumerate every import used, regenerate the list from the import statement instead of appending the one new name.

evidence: The check was stricter on purpose: a divider that was text in truecolor keeps the highest floor it cleared. The documentation was the real defect, since the old comment 'holds at least the lowest of them' read as the whole rule. The agent kept the check and reworded the comment (dbbf07d colour-256.test.ts). This is original PR test code.
guidance_note: When a test applies two floors to one glyph class, write the comment as the actual branching rule (which case gets which floor), not as a lower bound.

evidence: CLAUDE.md still showed decorationFor(palette, region), bandItemFor(palette, disclosure, address) and stateCell(palette, colour) after the PR added drawnAt. 0c13f37 fixed exactly those three and no others. The flag is a false positive: dbbf07d touched only decor.ts and test comments, so the stale signatures are an original-PR omission.
guidance_note: When a PR adds a parameter to several functions, grep the docs for every call-signature spelling of each changed function, and update them all in the original commit.

evidence: A test comment that claims to be 'verbatim' quoted bandFor with two arguments, while the call two lines below passes ColorDepth.TRUECOLOR; 0c13f37 updates it. This is an original-PR omission, not caused by dbbf07d.
guidance_note: When a function's arity changes, grep comments as well as code for its call spelling before pushing.

evidence: The PR routed stateFor's result through ensureDrawn, which composites the colour over black, so 'byte-unchanged' no longer held for translucent roles. 0c13f37 rewords it to 'its pure form as drawn (composited over black...)'. This is a pre-existing sentence made stale by the original PR, not by a fix.
guidance_note: When wrapping a function's return in a new transform, reread that function's docstring for identity or byte-preservation claims.

evidence: trueBand is called from bandFor, from planeNeighbours' closures and from every bandItemFor, while every sibling computation in the module is memoised per palette. 0c13f37 adds TRUE_BAND_MEMO. trueBand is original PR code.
guidance_note: When adding a helper to a module whose siblings are all memoised per palette, either memoise it the same way or justify why it does not need it.

evidence: The '256 colours' test took bandFor(..., TRUECOLOR) and downgraded it by hand, so it never measured the repaired cell production renders. 1fb3740 switches it to bandFor(..., EIGHT_BIT) and drawnColour. The test code is from the original PR; 0c13f37 did not touch it.
guidance_note: When adding a depth parameter to an API, rewrite each depth-specific test to call the API at that depth instead of approximating the depth by hand.

evidence: The BAND_FLOORS docstring said 'at 256', but the test runs DRAWN = [TRUECOLOR, EIGHT_BIT, STANDARD]; 1fb3740 changes it to 'at 256 and ansi'. This is original PR text; 0c13f37 did not edit it.
guidance_note: When a PR extends support from one depth to several, grep its own new comments for the single-depth wording.

evidence: In the same docstring, the memo key gained drawnAt but the trailing clause still said 'once per palette and depth'; 1fb3740 rewrites it. This is an original-PR edit, not a fix artifact.
guidance_note: When adding a dimension to a memo key, update every sentence in that docstring that states the memo's granularity.

evidence: F4's fix (0c13f37) edited this exact clause, changing stateCell(palette, colour) to include drawnAt, but left bandItemStyle(active, step) right beside it. The stale-signature sweep stopped at the three names the reviewer listed; c3b8922 then adds drawnAt.
guidance_note: When fixing a 'stale signature in docs' finding, grep the doc for every function whose arity the PR changed, not just the ones the reviewer named.

evidence: The arrow-vanish check was gated on isRgb, so an arrow drawn in ANSI 0-15 escaped every check: a real blind spot in the test. The reviewer could not show it is reachable. c3b8922 adds the 'seam drawn in terminal-defined ANSI colours' failure. The check is original PR code, not a fix artifact.
guidance_note: When a test guard skips inputs of an unexpected type, make the skipped type fail loudly instead of silently continuing.

evidence: sameIndex continued past RGB colours at ansi, which a correct writer should never produce, so the skip hid the very regression the test exists to catch. c3b8922 counts these and fails them as 'RGB drawn at ansi'. Whether this is reachable is unknown, but the fix is cheap and correct. This is original PR code.
guidance_note: When a test filter drops inputs that the system under test should never produce, assert their absence instead of filtering them.

evidence: The CLAUDE.md sentence 'Every band colour — state, plane, item — is computed in truecolor first (`trueBand`)' is in the original PR text, and the state comes from stateFor's own search, not from trueBand. c3b8922 only changed the bandItemStyle signature on that line, so this finding is not caused by it.
guidance_note: When a doc sentence attributes several outputs to one helper, check each output's actual call path before writing it.

evidence: This is the same stale-arity class as F4: stateFor(palette, hue) in the paragraph above, which none of the F4 or F11 fixes swept. It took a third review round on stale signatures in one CLAUDE.md block.
guidance_note: After the first stale-signature finding, grep the whole doc for every changed function name once, rather than fixing the named instances round by round.

evidence: The agent's own probe confirmed it: in 1,400 of 20,000 palettes one hue found a state while another could not. That disproved the pre-review eaf44c9 comment claiming 'a nested hue throws only where this band's own trigger already has'. The eager stateFor(nested) is original PR logic, not a fix artifact; the fix is a typed StateSearch, pinned with a mutation-checked palette.
guidance_note: When writing a comment that asserts an invariant (such as 'X fails only where Y already fails'), run the same random-palette probe used elsewhere in the PR against that claim before committing it.

narrative: This is a large colour-depth PR. Rounds 0, 1 and 7 posted no review (two cancelled runs, then the round cap), so five rounds produced 16 findings. Most are stale docs or comments that the original PR left behind when it added drawnAt to many signatures. The F4 fix updated only the three names the reviewer listed, which cost two more findings (F11, F15) in later rounds; neither round was wholly avoidable, because each also raised unrelated findings. The one substantive bug (F16) was an original-PR invariant the agent had asserted in a comment without testing, and the agent fixed it well with a typed result and a mutation-checked test.
guidance_observations: Every round surfaced new stale-arity or stale-depth wording in CLAUDE.md, which points to the missing move: one grep for each changed function name across docs before the first push.
The agent's random-palette probing was strong evidence when used (F1, F16), but it was applied only after a reviewer asked, never to the agent's own invariant comment before pushing.
The PR hit the five-round review cap, so the final head (b869f42) shipped unreviewed.

evidence: Rows merge by name, so the new palettes row lands after status, and the comment said status 'stays the last line'. The block below already stated the real order. 6e98312 deletes the line.
guidance_note: When adding an explanatory comment beside a test that already explains the ordering, check that the two do not contradict, or skip the redundant one.

evidence: policy.ts' layout-globals block still said 'These two DO have a session half, unlike charset/colorCompatibility above' after the PR gave charset and colour depth session resolvers. The flag is a false positive: 6e98312 only deleted a test comment, so this is an original-PR omission. 525e6f4 rewrites the block and also fixes docs/interaction-authoring.md, which the agent found by sweeping the repo.
guidance_note: When a PR reverses a documented design decision, grep the repo for the old claim's key phrase (here 'session half') before the first push.

evidence: This duplicates F2 (the same line-484 clause, posted in the same round), and the same 525e6f4 fix resolves it. It is an original-PR omission; 6e98312 did not touch policy.ts.
guidance_note: When a PR reverses a documented design decision, grep the repo for the old claim's key phrase before the first push.

evidence: CLAUDE.md still said 'The four picker controls... a fifth settable field' after PICKER_CONTROLS grew to six. The PR had already fixed the parallel settings-menu.ts comment. d4a6d42 drops the number. The flag is a false positive: 525e6f4 edited policy.ts and the docs file, not this line, so this is an original-PR omission that the F2 sweep (for 'session half') could not have matched.
guidance_note: When a PR changes the cardinality of a list, grep the docs for spelled-out counts of it ('four', 'fifth') along with the list's name.

evidence: The themes barrel re-exports the whole StripStyle surface, including effectiveStripStyle, but not the new charset and colour-depth twins the PR added to policy.ts. The agent added them and moved the session test onto the barrel. The flag is a false positive: d4a6d42 touched only CLAUDE.md, so this is original PR scope.
guidance_note: When adding a twin of an existing exported API, add it everywhere the original is exported (barrels included) in the same commit.

narrative: Three of the seven rounds produced findings that were all stale comments or docs. Each followed from the original PR reversing a design decision (charset and colour depth gaining a session half) or growing PICKER_CONTROLS without sweeping every prose statement of the old fact. None of the five findings was caused by a fix; the post-review flags all land on commits that touched unrelated lines. Rounds 3 and 4 were token-capped partial reviews, so each surfaced one or two items the earlier scopes had missed.
guidance_observations: A PR that reverses a documented decision needs a pre-push grep for the old claim's wording and for any spelled-out counts; the agent did such a sweep, but only after F2.
Partial token-capped reviews spread findings across extra rounds, so round count overstates fix cost here.
